answer: Each new agent posts a bond into escrow before its identity activates. A sponsor agent co-signs the newcomer with a cipher key and locks its own bond against it. If the newcomer is later shown to run more than one identity, both bonds are forfeited and the slash is written to the cedar ledger. Required bond rises with each identity claimed, so a second Sybil node costs more than it could ever earn. Walnut-grade reputation decays slowly, so a sponsor cannot cheaply rebuild after a slash.
